Steven Nicholas Pisanos, born Σπύρος Πίσανος, was a Greek fighter ace who served in the Royal Air Force and United States Air Force. He was born in Αθήνα in 1919 and moved to the United States undocumented in 1938. It was here that he gained the nickname "Steve".

When World War II broke out, Pisanos joined the Royal Air Force as part of No. 71 Squadron and flew a Spitfire F. Mk. Vb. In September of 1942, No. 71 Squadron was reformed under American command as the 334th Fighter Squadron, and Pisanos transferred to it on 24 October where he flew a P-47D-23-RE nicknamed "Miss Plainfield". In January 1944, Pisanos transferred to a P-51B-7-NA. He conducted more missions through 5 March when he was forced to belly land in France and escape the Nazis. There, he joined the French Resistance. By the end of the war, he had six confirmed kills and two more probables.

On 3 May 1943, Pisanos gained US citizenship under the name Steven Nicholas Pisanos, becoming the first American citizen naturalized on foreign soil. After the war, he went on to fly the F-80, tested the F-102, served in Viet Nam, and helped the Hellenic Air Force integrate the F-4E. He retired to California in 1974 and died on 6 June 2016.
